interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. landmarks.name: The Home of Dr Pepper (northbound)
landmarks.spoken: Billboard: Waco is the birthplace of Dr Pepper, the oldest major soft drink in America. It was mixed at a drugstore soda fountain here before Coke was even a gleam, and the museum occupies the old bottling plant.

landmarks.name: Texas Ranger Hall of Fame (northbound)
landmarks.spoken: Billboard: The Texas Ranger Hall of Fame, ahead in Waco. Two centuries of Rangers under one roof. Cheaper than meeting one on the shoulder.

landmarks.name: Magnolia (northbound)
landmarks.spoken: Billboard: Waco is home to Magnolia Market at the Silos. Chip and Joanna turned an old cotton mill into shiplap heaven, and the buses of shoppers have not stopped since.

landmarks.name: Waco Mammoth (northbound)
landmarks.spoken: Billboard: Waco Mammoth National Monument, ahead. In nineteen seventy-eight two teenagers hunting arrowheads found one big bone. The rest of the herd followed.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-23. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

interchanges.source: Exit ref, name and destination signs read from OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction nodes on a motorway or trunk way running along the leg's archived route, and the destination tags of this exit's own motorway_link ramps, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. at_mi derived: the mean of the exit's junction nodes (one per carriageway) projected onto that route, rescaled to the leg's miles: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_advisory_source: OpenStreetMap maxspeed:advisory on the motorway_link ways of this exit's ramp, per direction of travel (read; a directional suffix resolved from the way's drawn direction), the lowest on any branch of the ramp, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/ The forward ramp's length and terminal are kept from the previous bake, not the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: a baked street chain starts at that terminal.
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/ The forward ramp's length and terminal are kept from the previous bake, not the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: a baked street chain starts at that terminal.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

interchanges.source: Exit ref, name and destination signs read from OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction nodes on a motorway or trunk way running along the leg's archived route, and the destination tags of this exit's own motorway_link ramps, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. at_mi derived: the mean of the exit's junction nodes (one per carriageway) projected onto that route, rescaled to the leg's miles: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_advisory_source: OpenStreetMap maxspeed:advisory on the motorway_link ways of this exit's ramp, per direction of travel (read; a directional suffix resolved from the way's drawn direction), the lowest on any branch of the ramp, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-23. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

interchanges.source: Exit ref, name and destination signs read from OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction nodes on a motorway or trunk way running along the leg's archived route, and the destination tags of this exit's own motorway_link ramps, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. at_mi derived: the mean of the exit's junction nodes (one per carriageway) projected onto that route, rescaled to the leg's miles: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_control_source: OpenStreetMap highway=traffic_signals/highway=stop/highway=give_way node within 120 m of the walked terminal node where this exit's ramp chain ends (read; the walk supplies the node, the tag supplies the control), OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_advisory_source: OpenStreetMap maxspeed:advisory on the motorway_link ways of this exit's ramp, per direction of travel (read; a directional suffix resolved from the way's drawn direction), the lowest on any branch of the ramp, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-23. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

interchanges.source: Exit ref, name and destination signs read from OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction nodes on a motorway or trunk way running along the leg's archived route, and the destination tags of this exit's own motorway_link ramps, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. at_mi derived: the mean of the exit's junction nodes (one per carriageway) projected onto that route, rescaled to the leg's miles: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-23. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

interchanges.source: Exit ref, name and destination signs read from OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction nodes on a motorway or trunk way running along the leg's archived route, and the destination tags of this exit's own motorway_link ramps, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. at_mi derived: the mean of the exit's junction nodes (one per carriageway) projected onto that route, rescaled to the leg's miles: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_control_source: OpenStreetMap highway=traffic_signals/highway=stop/highway=give_way node within 120 m of the walked terminal node where this exit's ramp chain ends (read; the walk supplies the node, the tag supplies the control), OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

interchanges.source: Exit ref, name and destination signs read from OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction nodes on a motorway or trunk way running along the leg's archived route, and the destination tags of this exit's own motorway_link ramps, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. at_mi derived: the mean of the exit's junction nodes (one per carriageway) projected onto that route, rescaled to the leg's miles: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_control_source: OpenStreetMap highway=traffic_signals/highway=stop/highway=give_way node within 120 m of the walked terminal node where this exit's ramp chain ends (read; the walk supplies the node, the tag supplies the control), OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. traffic_aadt.source: Derived from FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) AADT and through-lane counts: median of HPMS sections snapping within 250 m of a 5-mile window of the leg, rounded to the nearest 500, lone dips between agreeing neighbours carried across. Sections queried from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view) and snapped to checked-in route geometry, accessed 2026-11-23: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-11-23: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-23. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

interchanges.source: Exit ref, name and destination signs read from OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction nodes on a motorway or trunk way running along the leg's archived route, and the destination tags of this exit's own motorway_link ramps, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. at_mi derived: the mean of the exit's junction nodes (one per carriageway) projected onto that route, rescaled to the leg's miles: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_control_source: OpenStreetMap highway=traffic_signals/highway=stop/highway=give_way node within 120 m of the walked terminal node where this exit's ramp chain ends (read; the walk supplies the node, the tag supplies the control), OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/ The backward ramp's length and terminal are kept from the previous bake, not the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: a baked street chain starts at that terminal.
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/ The backward ramp's length and terminal are kept from the previous bake, not the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: a baked street chain starts at that terminal.

'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-23. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

state_miles.source: derived 2026-11-05: the leg's archived route geometry intersected with OpenStreetMap state and province boundary relations (boundary=administrative, admin_level=4); at_mi = cumulative geometry distance at each boundary crossing, rescaled to leg miles; state miles = differences of those boundaries. OpenStreetMap, boundary relations read from the OpenStreetMap API on 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/.

interchanges.source: Exit ref, name and destination signs read from OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction nodes on a motorway or trunk way running along the leg's archived route, and the destination tags of this exit's own motorway_link ramps, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. at_mi derived: the mean of the exit's junction nodes (one per carriageway) projected onto that route, rescaled to the leg's miles: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_control_source: OpenStreetMap highway=traffic_signals/highway=stop/highway=give_way node within 120 m of the walked terminal node where this exit's ramp chain ends (read; the walk supplies the node, the tag supplies the control), OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

hpms_terrain.name: rolling
hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-08-19: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

interchanges.source: OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction exit ref and destination sign tags on the leg's Interstate shield, snapped to checked-in OSRM route geometry, accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from the gore in a local Geofabrik extract, accessed 2026-06-23. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_advisory_source: OpenStreetMap maxspeed:advisory on the motorway_link way at this exit (read; directional suffix resolved from OSM way direction into leg direction), from a local Geofabrik extract, accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included; direction from the ramp's first edge against the leg. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. Local Geofabrik extract accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. Local Geofabrik extract accessed 2026-06-23: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

interchanges.source: Exit ref, name and destination signs read from OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction nodes on a motorway or trunk way running along the leg's archived route, and the destination tags of this exit's own motorway_link ramps, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. at_mi derived: the mean of the exit's junction nodes (one per carriageway) projected onto that route, rescaled to the leg's miles: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-08-19: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-23. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

interchanges.source: Exit ref, name and destination signs read from OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction nodes on a motorway or trunk way running along the leg's archived route, and the destination tags of this exit's own motorway_link ramps, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. at_mi derived: the mean of the exit's junction nodes (one per carriageway) projected onto that route, rescaled to the leg's miles: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_control_source: OpenStreetMap highway=traffic_signals/highway=stop node on a motorway_link way within 1400 m of this exit's junctions, read from the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19; no control stood at a walked terminal: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_advisory_source: OpenStreetMap maxspeed:advisory on the motorway_link ways of this exit's ramp, per direction of travel (read; a directional suffix resolved from the way's drawn direction), the lowest on any branch of the ramp, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

interchanges.source: Exit ref, name and destination signs read from OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction nodes on a motorway or trunk way running along the leg's archived route, and the destination tags of this exit's own motorway_link ramps, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. at_mi derived: the mean of the exit's junction nodes (one per carriageway) projected onto that route, rescaled to the leg's miles: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

interchanges.source: Exit ref, name and destination signs read from OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction nodes on a motorway or trunk way running along the leg's archived route, and the destination tags of this exit's own motorway_link ramps, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. at_mi derived: the mean of the exit's junction nodes (one per carriageway) projected onto that route, rescaled to the leg's miles: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_advisory_source: OpenStreetMap maxspeed:advisory on the motorway_link ways of this exit's ramp, per direction of travel (read; a directional suffix resolved from the way's drawn direction), the lowest on any branch of the ramp, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-20. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

interchanges.source: Exit ref, name and destination signs read from OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction nodes on a motorway or trunk way running along the leg's archived route, and the destination tags of this exit's own motorway_link ramps, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. at_mi derived: the mean of the exit's junction nodes (one per carriageway) projected onto that route, rescaled to the leg's miles: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_advisory_source: OpenStreetMap maxspeed:advisory on the motorway_link ways of this exit's ramp, per direction of travel (read; a directional suffix resolved from the way's drawn direction), the lowest on any branch of the ramp, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-23. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

interchanges.source: Exit ref, name and destination signs read from OpenStreetMap highway=motorway_junction nodes on a motorway or trunk way running along the leg's archived route, and the destination tags of this exit's own motorway_link ramps, OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. at_mi derived: the mean of the exit's junction nodes (one per carriageway) projected onto that route, rescaled to the leg's miles: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_far_end_source: derived: this exit's motorway_link chains walked from every gore within 500 m of its junction nodes, both carriageways, in the OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19. 'motorway' means every chain merges onto a highway=motorway way; 'surface' means at least one chain ends off the motorway network: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_length_source: derived from OpenStreetMap geometry: summed node-to-node distance along this exit's motorway_link way(s), from the gore node where the ramp leaves the motorway to the nearest node where it ends (a public road -- trunk to residential, not a service or private way -- or a dead end, else a motorway merge). Per direction of travel: the gore nearest the exit's junction nodes whose first ramp edge runs that way. Starts at the OSM diverge, at or near the gore, so any deceleration lane before it is not included. Screened: under 300 ft or over 1.5 mi dropped, not clamped. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
interchanges.ramp_terminal_source: read from OpenStreetMap topology: the node where the same walk that measures ramp_length ends (the public crossroad or dead end the motorway_link way reaches), per direction of travel. Only baked beside a length that passed its screen, and never for a ramp that ends in a merge. OpenStreetMap planet file of 2026-10-19: https://www.openstreetmap.org/
